input:
Basis
The absorber has the function of removing the key component from the feed gas by means of absorption into a circulating amine solvent. The design throughput for the unit is 34 t per day of feed gas, and the removal duty is 90% of the key component that is present in the feed, measured between the feed gas as it enters and the treated gas as it leaves the absorber. The solvent circulates continuously between the absorber and its regeneration step: lean solvent enters at the top of the column, rich solvent leaves from the bottom carrying with it the component that has been absorbed, and the treated gas leaves from the overhead. It should be noted that the basis holds the duty on the absorber itself; the regeneration step is sized in order to return the solvent at the lean loading which the absorber basis assumes, and the performance that is stated in this report is therefore conditional upon that return condition actually being met in operation. The wetted parts are manufactured in 316L stainless steel, and the basis states this grade once, at this point; the materials section of the report works from the statement that has been made here. The feed composition and the operating pressure and temperature are taken as given for the purposes of the design, and the report does not revisit them. Performance is stated in terms of the removal of the key component only; any other components that are absorbed alongside it form part of the solvent duty but do not form part of the removal figure that has been stated.
Sizing
The column has been sized on the basis of the gas and liquid traffic that is established by the basis, together with the degree of contact that is needed in order to achieve the removal that has been stated. The diameter is determined by the gas rate, taken together with the liquid rate that the solvent circulation imposes at the removal duty, and it has been checked against flooding in order to ensure that the operating point sits below the flood point with the margin which good practice in amine service requires on account of the foaming tendency of the solvent. The packed or trayed height is determined by the mass-transfer requirement: the separation is expressed in terms of transfer units or stages, the height of a unit or of a stage is taken from the performance of the packing or trays in amine service, and the two are then combined in order to arrive at the contact height that the shell is required to contain. The solvent circulation is set by the removal duty and by the loading which the solvent is permitted to pick up between its lean and its rich states; a higher circulation makes the contact requirement easier to satisfy but increases the regeneration duty, and the sizing adopts the balance which the basis figures imply. An allowance has been made within the height for distribution, for redistribution and for the disengaging spaces at the two ends of the column, and the nozzles have been sized on the same traffic as the shell itself. It should be emphasised that the sizing is a design-point sizing: it establishes the vessel at the throughput and duty which have been stated, and it does not, by itself, establish the performance of the unit away from that point.
Materials
The wetted parts of the absorber are manufactured in the stainless steel that is named in the basis, and this choice is governed by the nature of amine service. Amine solvents are corrosive in proportion to their loading and to their temperature, and the degradation products which accumulate in a circulating solvent tend to add to the attack, so that the rich end of the circuit, where the loading and the temperature are at their highest in combination, represents the most exposed part of the whole system. The grade that is named in the basis is resistant to that service in circumstances where carbon steel would corrode at a rate that would shorten inspection intervals and would contaminate the solvent with corrosion products. The internals are specified in the same grade as the shell in those places where they are wetted, whilst non-wetted parts, supports and external attachments follow ordinary pressure-vessel practice appropriate to the design conditions. Welding and fabrication follow the vessel code that applies to the grade, with the solution-annealed condition being preserved in those places where forming or welding would otherwise sensitise the material. The materials statement that is made here covers the absorber and its internals; the solvent circuit beyond the column, the regeneration equipment and the interconnecting lines are all covered by their own statements elsewhere in the design, and nothing in this section should be taken as extending the grade of the absorber to those items.
Risks
There are two items which stand open at the close of the design, and it should be clearly stated that neither of them is resolved within this report. The first of these is the fouling of the internals. The feed gas carries solids and heavy ends into the column, the degradation of the solvent contributes solids of its own, and the deposits which form on the packing or on the trays act to reduce the contact which the sizing assumes and to raise the pressure drop across the column. The design states the duty on the basis of clean internals; the rate at which performance will fall away as fouling builds up, and the cleaning interval at which the service will eventually settle, are operating questions which the design figures are not able to answer, and the item accordingly stays open until it is closed by operating data or by a fouling allowance that is agreed with the solvent supplier. The second open item is turndown. The sizing is a design-point sizing, and at reduced levels of throughput the distribution of liquid over the packing or the trays deteriorates and the efficiency of contact falls, so that removal at low rates is not established by the design-point figures. The extent to which the absorber can be turned down while still meeting the removal that has been stated is not determined in this report, and the operating range of the unit is therefore stated at the design point only, with the turndown item being held open for the operating envelope study which follows the design.
